reason: Chest pain is a listed sign of cardiac distress that meets the necessity condition, and the trip was from her residence to a hospital. Supplier approval is not shown in the facts.

findings.claim: Chest pain documented as the reason for transport meets the medical-necessity presumption.
findings.quote: Exhibits signs and symptoms of acute respiratory distress or cardiac distress such as shortness of breath or chest pain

findings.claim: Hospital destination is presumed appropriate.
findings.quote: Because all duly licensed hospitals and SNFs are presumed to be appropriate sources of health care
findings.case_fact: On April 17, 2011, the beneficiary was transported from her residence to a hospital.

reason: Multiple therapy disciplines, physician involvement and measurable improvement are shown, and the 3-hour figure is not the only way to show intensity. Exact daily therapy minutes are not settled by the facts.

findings.claim: PT and OT were both provided, satisfying the multiple-discipline criterion.
findings.quote: The patient must require the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines

findings.claim: OT was also provided on most days.
findings.quote: one of which must be physical or occupational therapy
findings.case_fact: Occupational therapy was provided almost every day for periods of time totaling between 15 and 120 minutes per day.

findings.claim: Intensity can be shown other than by 3 hours/day, so the exact minutes need not be decisive.

findings.claim: Physician contact asserted daily, exceeding the 3 days/week visit standard.

findings.claim: Patient made measurable functional gains.

reason: The facts show a caregiver giving oral medications and insulin, which the manual says is not skilled nursing, and nothing shows another qualifying skilled need. Skilled observation need during the period is UNKNOWN.

findings.case_fact: the beneficiary had a caregiver who provided assistance with activities of daily living as well as the administration of oral medications

findings.claim: Patient must need a qualifying skilled service; the facts only show a stable condition and a nursing visit schedule.
findings.quote: The patient must need one of the following types of services
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary was discharged from home health care on October 17, 2008, based on the general stability of her blood sugar

reason: Nurses drew blood for prothrombin/INR while the physician was adjusting the Coumadin dose, and also performed observation and teaching under a plan of care with specified visit frequency; this fits the skilled nursing criteria in the passages.

findings.claim: Prothrombin monitoring is reasonable and necessary where dosage is being adjusted.
findings.quote: Where the documentation shows that the dosage is being adjusted, monitoring would be reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: based on this data, his physician modified the Coumadin dosages twice

findings.claim: Skilled observation is supported while a drug regimen may need modification.
findings.quote: Skilled observation is needed to determine whether the new drug regimen should be modified
findings.case_fact: the nurses also did regular cardiovascular and pulmonary checks, including checks for oxygen saturation as needed

findings.claim: Plan of care specified service type and frequency.
findings.quote: The orders on the plan of care must indicate the type of services to be provided to the patient
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary’s physician ordered skilled nursing care once in the initial week and then twice a week for four weeks

reason: The passages only say BLS is covered when ambulance transport is medically necessary, and the facts show a transport for nausea with a caregiver who could not use her SUV; nothing shown establishes that other transport was contraindicated, so necessity is UNKNOWN/unsupported.

findings.claim: BLS coverage depends on medical necessity.
findings.quote: the provision of medically necessary supplies and services
findings.case_fact: concerning Basic Life Support ambulance transportation (A0429-RH)

findings.claim: Transport must itself be medically reasonable and necessary; here the reason was nausea, treated and released.
findings.quote: provided that ambulance transportation itself was medically reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: Testimony presented during the hearing indicated that transport was in fact due to nausea

reason: Stable vitals and the appellant's concession that ground transport to a closer hospital was reasonable mean air transport was not shown necessary, so payment is limited to the ground ambulance amount; mileage beyond the nearest capable facility is not covered.

findings.claim: If ground would have sufficed, air transport is paid at the ground rate.
findings.quote: ground ambulance transport would have sufficed, payment for the air ambulance transport is based on the amount payable for ground ambulance transport
findings.case_fact: ground transportation to a closer hospital was reasonable

findings.claim: Air coverage requires a condition needing rapid transport that ground could not provide; vitals were stable.
findings.quote: The beneficiary’s medical condition required immediate and rapid ambulance transportation that could not have been provided by ground ambulance
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s vital signs were stable at the time of transfer

findings.claim: Air coverage requires that the nearest hospital with appropriate facilities be hard to reach, and a closer facility existed.
findings.quote: Great distances or other obstacles are involved in getting the patient to the nearest hospital with appropriate facilities
findings.case_fact: there was a closer facility equipped to treat the beneficiary’s medical needs than the one to which the beneficiary was transported

reason: A hospital-to-hospital transfer is separately payable under Part B when coverage criteria are met, and the transfer was recommended by the neurosurgeon for a hemorrhagic stroke. Whether a nearer capable hospital existed is UNKNOWN from the facts, so nothing shown defeats coverage.

findings.claim: A transfer between providers is payable as a Part B ambulance transport if criteria are met.
findings.quote: is also payable as a Part B ambulance transport, provided all program coverage criteria are met
findings.case_fact: Advanced Medical Transport of Central Illinois transported the beneficiary from Proctor Hospital to OSF Saint Francis Medical Center

findings.claim: Destination must be a capable facility; the family needed neurosurgical evaluation there.
findings.quote: that is capable of furnishing the required level and type of care for the beneficiary's illness or injury
findings.case_fact: the family did not know whether surgical intervention was warranted until after the beneficiary had been evaluated by the neurosurgeon at St. Francis

reason: The cardiologist states ambulance transport with a cardiac monitor was absolutely necessary given the recent pacemaker surgery and dependency, which supports medical necessity despite the walking comment. Whether the destination was the nearest capable facility is UNKNOWN.

findings.claim: Coverage requires medical necessity; the cardiologist attests necessity for monitored transport.
findings.quote: only if medical necessity and other program coverage criteria are met

findings.claim: Transport must be medically reasonable and necessary; the contrary evidence is that he could walk.
findings.quote: provided that the ambulance transportation was medically reasonable and necessary and all other coverage requirements are met

findings.claim: Recent pacemaker surgery supports a heightened cardiac risk during transport.
findings.quote: that is capable of furnishing the required level and type of care for the beneficiary's illness or injury
findings.case_fact: Three days earlier, he had undergone surgery for the removal and replacement of an infected pacemaker and generator

reason: Daily OT and PT (multiple disciplines), complex medical needs, and clear measurable functional and medical improvement support reasonable and necessary IRF care. Therapy hours and physician visit frequency are UNKNOWN from the facts.

findings.claim: Multiple therapy disciplines were planned.
findings.quote: The patient must require the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines
findings.case_fact: The initial IRF treatment plan included providing daily occupational and physical therapy

findings.claim: Measurable practical improvement in function occurred.
findings.quote: a measurable, practical improvement in the patient’s functional condition can be accomplished within a predetermined and reasonable period of time
findings.case_fact: had moved from total assist for walking to modified independence in walking

findings.claim: Patient was able to participate in and benefit from the program.
findings.quote: patients must be able to actively participate in and benefit from the intensive rehabilitation therapy program
findings.case_fact: abdominal complaints improved, her energy improved, her eating improved, and she gained five pounds

findings.claim: Medical management needs were substantial at admission.

reason: The record shows the inpatient status was reverted to observation as an error and the discharge summary says overnight observation, and observation orders are not treated as meeting inpatient admission requirements. findings.claim: Observation-type orders are not inpatient admission orders.
findings.quote: such orders will not be treated as meeting the inpatient admission requirements
findings.case_fact: Decision to change from observation to inpt status was made in ERROR.

findings.claim: The admission order is the evidence of the decision to admit to inpatient status; the discharge summary says observation.
findings.quote: The admission order is evidence of the decision by the ordering practitioner to admit the beneficiary to inpatient status.

findings.claim: Admission is a medical judgment based on severity; the ED note supports clinical concern but does not create an inpatient order.

reason: The manual says ambulance service to a physician-directed clinic is not covered, the run sheet calls the destination a clinic, and the appellant's claim that it was a hospital or SNF is only his assertion with no listing or other support in the facts.

findings.claim: Ambulance service to a clinic is not covered.
findings.quote: Ambulance service to a physician’s office or a physician-directed clinic is not covered.
findings.case_fact: the destination to which the appellant was taken was described as a “clinic.”

findings.claim: A SNF must be a listed participating SNF or meet the statutory definition; the appellant only contends this.

reason: The beneficiary could not leave home without taxing effort and had many functional limitations, and the only absences were infrequent adult day care and doctor visits, which the manual says do not defeat homebound status. findings.claim: Infrequent absences do not defeat homebound status.
findings.quote: the patient may nevertheless be considered homebound if the absences from the home are infrequent
findings.case_fact: absences from the home, though infrequent, included adult day care and doctor visits.

findings.claim: Infrequent or short absences do not disqualify.
findings.quote: shall not so disqualify an individual if the absence is of an infrequent or of relatively short duration

findings.claim: Longitudinal clinical information on functional limitations supports a taxing-effort finding.

findings.claim: Formal inpatient admission with expectation of a stay spanning two midnights makes one an inpatient.
findings.quote: formally admitted as inpatient with the expectation that he or she will require hospital care that is expected to span at least two midnights
findings.case_fact: He was initially placed in observation status but subsequently admitted to inpatient status.

findings.claim: Severity of signs and symptoms is an admission factor; new T-wave inversion was noted.
findings.quote: The severity of the signs and symptoms exhibited by the patient
findings.case_fact: new T-wave inversion was noted

findings.claim: Medical predictability of adverse events is an admission factor; he had low blood pressure with bradycardia.
findings.quote: The medical predictability of something adverse happening to the patient
findings.case_fact: he experienced brief low blood pressure with bradycardia

reason: The cardiac transfer from a hospital lacking specialist care is the kind of air transport the manual covers, but the appellant's own statement indicates a Texas facility was available and was not tried first. findings.claim: Transferring hospital lacked the needed specialty (cardiac) services.
findings.quote: the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient
findings.case_fact: The transfer occurred so that the beneficiary would be treated in a hospital where specialist cardiologist services were available.

findings.claim: Patient was becoming unstable, supporting that ground transport risked her health.
findings.quote: transportation by ground ambulance would endanger the beneficiary’s health
findings.case_fact: as the beneficiary became progressively “more unstable,”

findings.case_fact: before trying the facility in TX that Medicare preferred

findings.claim: If a nearer hospital could have treated her, air payment is capped at the distance to it.
findings.quote: the air transport payment is limited to the rate for the distance from the point of pickup to that nearer hospital
findings.case_fact: Beaver County Memorial Hospital did contact two other hospitals before transferring the beneficiary to Via Christi

reason: Skilled speech-language pathology for dysphagia was ordered by the physician, based on documented swallowing deficits, and produced documented improvement; the manual says coverage does not depend solely on potential for improvement.

findings.claim: SLP is covered when it is reasonably expected to improve or maintain feeding ability.
findings.quote: where it is reasonably expected that the skilled service will improve, maintain, or prevent or slow further deterioration
findings.case_fact: The therapy notes of the second four week period record “steady improvements,”

reason: Weekly aide and nursing hours (about seven) are well under the part-time limit, her day care absences fall under the adult day care exception, and other caregivers do not defeat coverage. findings.claim: Attendance at a qualifying adult day care program does not defeat homebound status.

findings.quote: an adult day care center must be either licensed or certified by the State or accredited by a private accrediting body

findings.quote: For any home health services to be covered by Medicare, the patient must meet the qualifying criteria as specified in §30

reason: The surgery was a large, complicated hernia repair with documented pulmonary risk and a stay across two nights, so it is not a minor short outpatient procedure. The facts do not show the inpatient admission order, which is UNKNOWN.

reason: The services described (medication, glucose monitoring, diet and fluids) were being done by family and aides, and the manual says services that unskilled caregivers can safely perform are not covered. findings.quote: Gait evaluation and training furnished to a patient whose ability to walk has been impaired by neurological, muscular or skeletal abnormality

findings.case_fact: Upon discharge, this score had improved to 18/28, signifying a moderate fall risk.
